text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein and U.S. President Clinton discuss the latest developments and the tragic situation in Iraq; the king emphasises the need to abide by signed peace accords between the Israelis and Palestinians.
- Clinton says comprehensive peace in Middle East cannot be attained without King Hussein's strong influence.
- King Hussein stresses the need for comprehensive peace and the status of Jerusalem; says supports the Palestinian people and the need to implement the Oslo accord.
- A new system for bonuses and incentives for teachers and recruitment of 2,500 teachers, says education minister.
- Acting prime minister says that amending the election law should be in harmony with the administrative changes in the kingdom.
- U.S. aid to Jordan topped $1.6 billion since 1990.
- Housing Bank heads towards comprehensive commercial banking alongside real estate business, says chairman.
- New measures to streamline export license permits.
- King, Clinton discuss means to end crisis in peace process, White House talks focus on Palestinian-Israeli impasse as well as Jordanian-US relations.
